extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.inLanguage: English, Latin, Gujarati, and 93 other languages
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Crawlers were designed to fetch all PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed, resulting in 73,285 conference journal and workshop papers. The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing recently added papers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing section names, merged paragraphs, the mixing of footnotes with texts, misidentifying texts as table captions, and missing figures and tables (especially in-line equations) due to GROBID extraction limitations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ACL Anthology and Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG)
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Incorrect metadata from PDF extraction was replaced with metadata from the ACL Anthology. Model predictions were extrapolated and integrated as silver-labeled topic information.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The OCL corpus is linked with the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) using its Graph API to connect an OCL document to its corresponding document in S2AG to enrich it with external information such as citations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. GROBID was used for full-text extraction from PDF files into S2ORC-JSON format. PDFFigures was used to extract figures and tables. A public language detection toolkit was used with title and abstract as inputs to detect language.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Objective topics were assigned to each CL paper. A pre-trained language model (PLM) based topic classification method was trained on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground truth topic labels crawled from conference websites. The model predictions were then extrapolated and integrated as silver-labeled topic information.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: BART-large-MNLI, SciBERT, SPECTER, language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates to process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology by monitoring changes in URLs. The plan is to update OCL by year to keep it alive, with an ultimate goal to provide extraction APIs to ACL Anthology to host the data there.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There is a significant disparity in coverage among languages, with numerous low-resource languages remaining underrepresented. There is also a bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics like Machine Translation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: It is a small-scale collection focusing only on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology, not a comprehensive corpus. It is an unlabeled resource lacking annotations for specific tasks. Full text quality is influenced by GROBID's inherent limitations in extracting formatting information, tables, and figures from PDFs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Temporal topic trends analysis, document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models, fine-tuning general LLMs, summarization, related work generation, information/knowledge extraction from specific sections, and analyzing historical language change.
